title: Try-to-Prod: 15m value scripts and rate framing
content:
Purpose: quick, testable messaging and scripts to get an engineer from curiosity -> instrumented call -> billing in ~15 minutes. Focus: developer-first voice, explicit economics, low-friction success moments.

Quick thesis (one line): ship a working call in minutes, see latency/cost in your console, keep the bill predictable. Confidence comes from speed + transparency.

Target personas (primary -> secondary):
- Staff/Principal engineers evaluating infra for in-product LLM features (concerned with latency, tail p99, integration complexity)
- ML engineers onboarding model variants and looking for cost controls (quantization, batching, caching)
- Platform/Infra leads evaluating vendor lock + operations overhead

Top messaging pillars (short hooks):
- 15m to a real call: SDK + starter project, example input, streaming responses 
- Predictable unit economics: per-token + per-embedding with console breakdowns and a cost estimator init call
- Production controls from day one: routing policies, canary rollout, and automatic fallback to smaller variants
- Dev-first observability: token-level latency and cost traces in the console and SDK telemetry

User journey: "Try to Prod in 15" (short flow to iterate in UI/marketing)
1) Create free account -> default API key (auto-provision short-lived key)
2) Select starter app (chat, summarizer, semantic search) – github template clones to user repo
3) Run local quickstart: SDK install + single example call (command shown) -> returns streaming response
4) Console shows the call: tokens, latency breakdown, estimated cost line-item
5) Click "promote to route" -> generate route config (pin model version, set SLOs)
6) Toggle canary or scale -> begin measuring QPS and cost per 1k tokens in Console metrics

Quickstart copy snippets (for CLI/README/banners) — keep short, actionable, engineer tone:
- "From zero to a streaming call in under 15 minutes. No infra. No surprise bills."
- "Run one command, get a live response, see exact token and latency cost in the Console."
- "Use the sample app or bring your prompt set — pin a model, set SLOs, ship."

Pricing language drafts (for UX & onboarding screens)
- Guiding principle: be explicit, anchor to a simple unit, show transparency.
- Suggested on-boarding panel text: "Pay-as-you-go: $X per 1k prompt tokens, $Y per 1k generated tokens, $Z per 1k embedding units. Free trial credits for 30 days. Console shows exact token split for each call."
- Sample conversational phrasing (short): "Estimate cost before you call — toggle model size and sequence length to see price delta. We recommend enabling prefix caching for high hit-rate workloads to reduce generated token cost."
- Billing experiment A: show "estimated per-call cost" inline vs A/B control showing only per-1k token rates. Metric: conversion to first paid project.

Competitive notes (snapshots to paste into battlecards)
- CloudAIX (managed endpoints): strong enterprise integrations, weaker dev UX. Typical objection: "we can get similar latency on their infra but need our infra code". Rebuttal: "Redwood gives the same latency profiles with a developer flow and built-in rollout/traceback so ops overhead is lower."
- OpenRuntime++ (self-hosted): cheapest at scale but heavy ops. Rebuttal: "If you want bare-metal control, Redwood Private; if you want less ops, Hosted + Optimize gives similar unit economics for common workloads via batching + caching suggestions."
- API-only startups (fast simple APIs): great dev onboarding but opaque pricing and variable tail latency. Rebuttal: "We surface tail metrics and cost per token so you can debug and optimize before scale."

Differentiators to highlight in copy:
- explicit cost visibility per call (token split + micro-latency timeline)
- fast path from trial -> instrumented route -> SLA-backed dedicated (clear upgrade path)
- automated suggestions that reduce unit cost (batching, quantization profiles)

Objections + rebuttals (short, usable in sales snippets)
- "Your pricing is complex" -> "We show an exact per-call estimate and console breakdown; pick flat reserved capacity when you want predictability."
- "Vendor lock concerns" -> "We export model artifacts & configs, support private deployments and clear upgrade/downgrade model pinning."
- "We run on-prem today" -> "Private package + VPC control plane, same API surface, same rollout primitives — minimal code changes."

Microcopy examples for Console and SDK errors/notifications
- On quickstart success toast: "Nice — sample call succeeded. View cost & latency in Console > Recent Calls."
- If estimated cost > threshold: "Heads up — this call will cost ~${{est}}. Consider smaller model or reduced max_tokens."

Experiment ideas (short list for growth + product)
- Quickstart CTA variants: "Try a live call" vs "View estimated cost first". Measure: demo-to-instrumented-call conversion.
- Pricing anchor experiment: show monthly reserved vs pay-go calculator upfront vs hidden until project creation. Metric: upgrade to reserved purchase.
- Guided optimization flow: after 100 calls, nudge user with "We estimate 32% saving with prefix caching". Metric: adoption of suggested config and reducing per-token spend.

Metrics to instrument (for success):
- Time-to-first-successful-call (target < 15m)
- Time-to-first-route (promote to route)
- Conversion from free trial -> first paid project
- Average cost per 1k generated tokens by cohort (to detect pricing friction)
- Feature adoption: prefix caching, canary rollouts, reserved capacity purchases

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- final pricing anchors: need engineering to confirm baseline per-1k rates for desktop vs server models (ENG ask: pricing matrix needed).
- decide whether to show "estimated per-call cost" by default or behind a toggle (growth experiment).
- verify copy constraints for EU customers (VAT phrasing + localization).
- get legal sign-off on "no surprise bill" phrasing.

Appendix: sample quickstart command + minimal code snippet (for README)
- one-liner (bash): `pip install redwood-sdk && REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test redwood run-sample chat --file sample-prompts.json`
- minimal node call (snippet for README):
  const r = require('redwood');
  const c = new r.Client(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY);
  const res = await c.chat.create({ model: 'rw-medium-v1', messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Summarize last quarter sales notes.'}] });
  console.log(res.stream());

Voice notes (tone guidance):
- Keep it engineer-first: assume comfort with command line, show code early. Avoid marketing hype.
- Be explicit about limits and costs — engineers dislike surprises.
- Use brief hero proof points on landing: "Streaming, deterministic routing, cost transparency."

Next steps (owner + collaborators):
- [Samira] lock price anchors with finance (due 2024-10-04)
- [Diego] draft quickstart README + sample app (due 2024-10-11)
- [Aisha] design Console CTA and cost-estimate UX mocks (due 2024-10-09)
- [Liam] wire up experiment tracking: Quickstart CTA variants (due 2024-10-15)

Notes: rough, iterate with product & finance. Keep copy short, testable, instrumented.

End of doc.
